items.stem: You need precise control over two subplots that share an x-axis. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Create a Figure and Axes with plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True) and call methods on each Axes
options.rationale: Correct: the object-oriented API gives explicit per-Axes control and shared axes.

options.text: Call plt.plot() repeatedly and hope the state machine targets the right subplot
options.rationale: The implicit state machine makes targeting the intended subplot error-prone.

options.text: Make two separate figures and paste them together in an image editor
options.rationale: That loses shared axes and reproducibility.

options.text: Use a single Axes and overplot both series regardless of scale
options.rationale: Overplotting different scales on one Axes misleads the reader.

items.explanation: Correct: the object-oriented API gives explicit per-Axes control and shared axes.

items.stem: Which TWO choices improve the accessibility of a chart? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: colour-blind-safe palettes keep categories distinguishable.

options.text: Add direct labels or patterns so meaning does not rely on colour alone
options.rationale: Correct: redundant encoding supports readers who cannot distinguish colours.

options.text: Encode five categories with closely spaced rainbow hues
options.rationale: Rainbow hues are hard to distinguish and not perceptually uniform.

options.text: Remove the legend and axis titles to reduce clutter
options.rationale: Removing labels harms comprehension, not accessibility.

items.explanation: Correct: colour-blind-safe palettes keep categories distinguishable.

items.stem: A Seaborn figure-level function (e.g. relplot) returns which object that controls the whole figure?

options.text: A FacetGrid-style object managing the figure and its facets
options.rationale: Correct: figure-level functions return a grid object that owns the figure.
That is what axes-level functions target, not figure-level ones.
The input may be a DataFrame; the return is not.

options.text: Nothing; it only draws to the current Axes
options.rationale: Figure-level functions create and return their own figure object.

items.explanation: Correct: figure-level functions return a grid object that owns the figure.
